qt: to the Commission Anna Bryłka (PfE) Subject:

Since mid-July, the Black Sea has been blockaded due to Russian attacks on merchant ships. According to information from Ukraine, consultations are ongoing with frontline countries and the EU regarding the transit of agricultural goods and increasing exports to the EU market. In this connection: 1.

Is the Commission conducting or planning to launch consultations with Ukraine on revising the DCFTA/Association Agreement or on increasing duty-free tariff quotas for imports of agricultural goods from Ukraine?

How does the Commission monitor and verify the process of aligning Ukrainian production standards with the EU’s stringent requirements, which is a fundamental condition for maintaining fair competition in the single market?
Does the Commission envisage mobilising financial or other instruments to mitigate the effects of the Black Sea blockade?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.10.2026) The Commission considers that the revised EU Ukraine Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area (DCFTA)1, in force since 29 October 2025, continues to provide a stable, reciprocal, and predictable trade regime for both EU and Ukrainian farmers. It is not planning consultations to revise the DCFTA. The Commission continues to monitor EU-Ukraine trade flows. Trade data so far proves the fair and balanced nature of the revised DCFTA. Pursuant to the revised DCFTA, Ukraine shall align its legislation to the relevant EU production standards by the end of 2028 and shall report annually on its progress. Ukraine is also aligning its national legislation to the EU acquis as part of the EU accession negotiations. Progress is assessed regularly. The Commission continues to monitor how the Ukrainian harvest develops, how this aligns with storage capacity and export needs. The Commission is in close contacts with the EU Member States neighbouring Ukraine to assess the needs for helping ensure alternative logistics routes via the Solidarity Lanes2. Budget support and derisking financial instruments for farmers are available under the Ukraine Facility3. With international donors, the Commission is supporting grain storage, logistics and the security of border crossing points.
